newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols mixed as futures see-saw.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols mixed as futures see-saw.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond implied volatilities ended mixed Thursday, with September firming as the underlying futures traded erratically.
September climbed about 0.2 point to 8.35 percent from the previous session after opening at 8.25 percent, boosted by nervous, choppy trading in the underlying futures, floor traders said.

July volatility edged down to 7.80 percent from the previous day's 7.90 percent, which analysts attributed to the options' expiration date falling before the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting July 1-2.

June Treasury bond futures ended 7/32 lower at 109-02 after failing in several attempts to breach key support at 108-30. Futures rallied in the last hour of trading after the FOMC minutes for the March 25 meeting were released, but the bounce was short-lived.

Around the time the minutes were released, a brokerage firm began aggressively bidding for the July 110-00 bond calls, buying about 2,000 of the options at premiums ranging from 29/64 to as high as 34/64, floor traders said.
The FOMC minutes said the central bankers voted unanimously to raise the federal funds rate by 1/4 point in March, but a few had argued for a larger increase.
The group also voted unanimously to adopt a symmetric policy stance before the May 20 meeting, which cheered the market initially, traders said.
However, they said the minutes gave a mixed message overall because they also highlighted the temporary nature of factors that were keeping labor costs subdued.
In Eurodollar options, large-scale buying of put options was the theme for a second day, floor traders said.
A U.S. brokerage house bought 10,000 September 93.75 puts in what was thought to be hedging against a position in one-year Treasury bills.
About 12,000 June 94.00 puts were purchased in a separate transaction that also was thought to be a downside hedge.
Eurodollar volatilities swung higher, with September rising 0.2 point to 9.0 percent and December gaining 0.4 point to 11.0 percent.
